- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 2024 (Q2 2024) and overestimates in late 2024 (Q3 2024), suggesting seasonal or calendar bias.
- Forecasts tend to be too low relative to recent history, especially after sharp price spikes — model fails to capture momentum or mean reversion in the short term.
- After a price spike, forecasts often overshoot and then drop too quickly, indicating poor handling of volatility clustering or momentum decay.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to recent price movements — especially when prices are trending downward, forecasts remain too high.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” sharp declines or rises, underreacting to sudden changes in the 30-day history.
- In periods of high volatility (e.g., 2024-05), model overreacts to recent highs and fails to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when recent history includes a strong upward trend — fails to recognize that momentum may persist longer than expected.
- Forecasts are often too conservative in the face of recent price increases, underestimating the probability of continuation or reversal.
